package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions integrated at time of attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The Picreel marketing script was compromised in a supply chain attack, resulting in the injection of MageCart web skimming code into websites that included Picreel, such as Forbes. The injected code steals payment data from site visitors, making the entire package malicious during the period of compromise.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into Picreel JavaScript (served to client browsers on victim sites)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into form submission events, collects payment and personal data from the form, and exfiltrates this data via HTTP POST to a malicious domain controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and sending sensitive data to an external, attacker-controlled domain is a classic sign of web skimming and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal marketing scripts should not access or exfiltrate payment or personal data from checkout forms. Legitimate analytics may collect anonymized data, but not full payment details.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect form data, but only to their own secure endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Reads all form data including payment fields
Sends data to an external, non-affiliated domain
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: MageCart group compromises Picreel's JavaScript supply chain and injects malicious skimming code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to all websites embedding Picreel.

attack_chain.action: Victim websites (e.g., Forbes) load the compromised Picreel script, which executes in visitors' browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs in the context of the victim website.

attack_chain.action: Injected MageCart code hooks into payment/checkout form submissions, collects sensitive data, and exfiltrates it to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into form submission events
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing form or payment data to untrusted domains
Unexpected modification of third-party marketing scripts
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in third-party JavaScript (e.g., Picreel) loaded from CDN or vendor
Presence of event listeners on sensitive forms not present in original code
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not affiliated with the website or payment processor
Connections to known MageCart infrastructure or previously identified malicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to payment or checkout forms and sends form data to external domains. Use content integrity checks (subresource integrity, hashes) on third-party scripts. Analyze network traffic from client browsers for suspicious POST requests containing sensitive data to unknown endpoints. Regularly audit third-party scripts for unauthorized modifications.
